gloss: to be attentive to others' needs; to be considerate

definitions.gloss: to be attentive; to notice what others need; to be considerate
definitions.explanation: To have one's attention reach the small things other people need before being asked. Literally 'one's attention goes around.' Usually a compliment, most often in the negative — {気|き}が{回|まわ}らなかった means 'it didn't occur to me.'

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はよく{気|き}が{回|まわ}る。
そこまで{気|き}が{回|まわ}らなかった。
examples.english: It didn't occur to me to go that far.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}なのに{細|こま}かいところまで{気|き}が{回|まわ}る{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: Even though he's new, he's the sort who notices the smallest things.

examples.japanese: {準備|じゅんび}に{追|お}われて、{お客|きゃく}さんの{飲|の}み{物|もの}まで{気|き}が{回|まわ}らなかった。
examples.english: I was so busy with the preparations that I didn't think as far as drinks for the guests.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {気|き} (attention) + が + {回|まわ}る (to go around).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- よく{気|き}が{回|まわ}る: to be very attentive (standard praise)
- {気|き}が{回|まわ}らない: to fail to notice, to not think of
- {細|こま}かいところまで{気|き}が{回|まわ}る: to notice even small details

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気|き}が{利|き}く: to be thoughtful — nearly synonymous; {気|き}が{利|き}く also describes objects and gifts as 'clever, well-chosen', which {気|き}が{回|まわ}る does not
- {気|き}を{使|つか}う: to be considerate — an effort the speaker consciously makes, often tiring; {気|き}が{回|まわ}る happens naturally
